# Layout revision report — Sample Hall A (40m x 30m)

> This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations.

## Summary

## Before / after

**Time the average visitor spent in crowded areas (≥ 2 p/m²): 16.82 s → 8.47 s (−49.7%)**; crowded person-seconds 3364 → 1693.

| Metric | Baseline (iteration 0) | Final (iteration 2) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Time the average visitor spent in crowded areas (≥ 2 p/m²)** | **16.82 s** | **8.47 s** | **−8.35 s (−49.7%)** |
| Crowded person-seconds (all visitors) | 3364 person-s | 1693 person-s | −1671 (−49.7%) |
| Peak crowded area (at one moment) | 26.8 m² | 11.8 m² | −15 m² (−56.1%) |
| Worst hotspot, mean density over the run | 1 p/m² | 1.16 p/m² | +0.16 p/m² (+16.2%) |
| p90 travel time | 279.2 s | 282.6 s | +3.4 s (+1.2%) |
| Completed fraction | 82.5% | 85.5% | +3 pt |
| Mean travel time | 206.4 s | 204.7 s | −1.7 s (−0.8%) |
| Hotspots | 4 | 5 | +1 |
| Validation errors | 0 | 0 | ±0 |
| Max density¹ | 3.69 p/m² | 3 p/m² | −0.69 p/m² (−18.7%) |

¹ Highest density any single grid cell reached at any instant; a momentary peak, shown for reference only. The agent compares and stops on the crowded time per visitor above.

Target: ≤ 10 s per visitor in crowded areas with no validation errors. An iteration counts as better only if it cuts that by at least 10% vs the best so far and its completion stays within 5 pt of the baseline.

Identical conditions for every iteration: scenario `browse`, 200 agents, 300 s, seed 42, density grid 2 m, crowded = ≥ 2 p/m² (fingerprint `c426fcb1`).

Stop reason: **target met** — crowded time 8.47 s/visitor (1693 person-s at ≥ 2 p/m²) ≤ target 10 s with no validation errors.

## Design brief (initial constraints)

Indoor hall with moderate attendance for its floor area: the standard aisle width and door clearance apply and booths are not yet pushed away from the entrance. The first simulation will show whether the entrance area needs more room.

- Default constraints kept.

Booth coordinates were then computed by the layout solver under these constraints.

## What changed and why

**Revision after iteration 0 → 1.** High-attraction booth B10 sits in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds.

- popular_door_distance 0 → 12 m

**Revision after iteration 1 → 2.** Hotspot #0 persists next to B10, which shares the zone with other high-attraction booths; moving it east separates their visitor crowds.

- B10 target (16.5, 13.5) → (22.5, 13.5)

## Iteration history

| Iteration | Crowded s/visitor | Crowded person-s | Peak crowded area (m²) | p90 travel (s) | Completed | Max density (p/m²) | Errors | Comparable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 16.82 | 3364 | 26.8 | 279.2 | 82.5% | 3.69 | 0 | yes |
| 1 | 13.53 | 2706 | 17.3 | 281.9 | 86.5% | 3.14 | 0 | yes |
| 2 | 8.47 | 1693 | 11.8 | 282.6 | 85.5% | 3 | 0 | yes |

## Assumptions

- Pedestrian metrics come from the engine's JuPedSim simulation; one scenario and seed per run, so results are a single sample, not a distribution.
- Booth popularity values are planning estimates of relative attraction, taken as given.
- A 2 m grid cell counts as crowded while its density is at or above 2 p/m²; crowded person-seconds add up the people standing in crowded cells, sampled once per second, and per visitor divides that by the visitors who entered. Max density is the single highest cell value at any instant; hotspot thresholds are the engine's. Travel times count finished agents only.
- Geometric checks cover booth/obstacle/door-clearance/aisle rules only; egress capacity, fire code and accessibility were not assessed.
- Analysis and revision proposals by `stub`; all metrics and coordinates in this report are computed by tools.

## Unconfirmed items

- Ceiling height not shown on plan (from floor plan)
- Emergency door D-emg swing direction unconfirmed (from floor plan)

---

_This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations._
